apoc-apoc:
The first word in the Greek text of Revelation is 'Ἀποκάλυψις', which:
  • when transliterated, is 'apocalypsis' … the source of the English word 'apocalypse';
  • but when translated, is an 'unveiling' or a 'revealing' of something hidden … that is, a 'revelation'!
transliterated:
[Back]
Transliteration is the process of changing the letters of a word from a text in another language (such as the ancient Koine Greek used in the NT) into the equivalent letters in English. This effectively makes the word 'readable' using equivalent sounds in the English language, but in no way translates the actual meaning of the word to an English equivalent.
Other examples of 'transliterated' words commonly found in the New Testament include:

  • 'amen' from ἀμήν (≈ amēn) which means 'truly', 'certainly' or 'so be it'
  • 'hallelujah' from ἁλληλουϊά (≈ hallēlouia) which means 'praise the LORD'
  • 'Christ' from Χριστός (≈ Christos) which means 'Anointed one'
  • 'baptise' from βαπτίζω (≈ baptizō) which means 'immerse', 'dip' or 'wash'
  • 'apostle' from ἀπόστολος (≈ apostolos) which means 'envoy' or 'sent one'

Such transliterated words effectively become 'loan words' in English where they often accrue meanings & connotations that were not present (or at least not predominant) in the original language.
This is certainly the case with 'apocalypse'!
translated:
[Back]
Translation is the process by which scholars determine what meanings the original words, phrases & sentences used in the ancient Koine Greek of the NT would have communicated to the original readers, & then writing English words, phrases & sentences which communicate as closely as possible that same meaning to modern English speakers & readers. Examples of 'translated' words commonly found in the New Testament include:

  • 'grace' from χάρις (≈ charis) which can refer to 'favour', 'kindness' or 'a gracious gift'
  • 'peace' from εἰρήνη (≈ eirēnē) which can refer to 'peace', 'harmony', 'wellbeing' or 'reconciliation'
  • faith from πίστις (≈ pistis) which can refer to 'faith', 'trust', 'belief', 'faithfulness' or 'fidelity'
  • 'love' from ἀγάπη (≈ agapē) which may refer to 'love', 'devotedness', 'generosity' or 'an unconditional positive regard for another'

Given the various nuances of anciemt words, a translator often uses different English words to translate the same Greek word at different points in a text to effectively express which nuances of meaning were intended by the original author.
apoc-media:
These books, radio broadcasts, TV series & movies (and even popular songs) tell stories that portray people in situations where they are:
  • trying to prevent the catastrophe, or
  • trying to survive the catastrophe, or
  • trying to survive in the 'post-apocalyptic' world after the catastrophe.
media-books:
[Back]
Significant examples of books telling 'apocalyptic' stories include:

  • Le Dernier Homme (The Last Man) (1805) by Jean-Baptiste de Grainville
  • The Last Man (1826) by Mary Shelley
  • After London (1885) by Richard Jefferies
  • The War of the Worlds (1898) by HG Wells
  • The Machine Stops (1909) by EM Forster
  • The Scarlet Plague (1912) by Jack London
  • Niels Klim's Journey Under the Ground / Metropolis (1925) by Thea von Harbou
  • The Shape of Things to Come (1933) by HG Wells
  • Earth Abides (1949) by George R Stewart
  • The Day of the Triffids (1951) by John Wyndham
  • I Am Legend (1954) by Richard Matheson
  • On the Beach (1957) by Nevil Shute
  • A Canticle for Leibowitz (1959) by WM Miller Jr.
  • The Stand (1978) by Stephen King
  • The Handmaid's Tale (1985) by Margaret Atwood
  • The Children of Men (1992) by P.D. James
  • The Road (2006) by Cormac McCarthy
  • World War Z (2006) by Max Brooks
media-books-Grainville:
[Back]
Jean-Baptiste François Xavier Cousin de Grainville was an ex-priest who merged traditional biblical apocalypse themes (inverting the Genesis account) with early concepts of science fiction, such as futuristic technology & global human extinction.

The last fertile couple om Earth are urged by the Spirit of the Earth to repopulate the world but they are confronted by Adam (the biblical first man) who has been sent by God to convince them not to prolong humanity's existence, as God has decreed that the human race must finally end.
media-books-Shelley:
[Back]
Shelley tells the story of a world destroyed by a global plague.
media-books-Jefferies:
[Back]
Jefferies tells perhaps the first post-apocalyptic story, in which nature reclaims England after an unspecified catastrophe.
media-books-Wells:
[Back]
Wells wrote this alien invasion story which became a massive milestone in apocalyptic fiction. It fundamentally shifted how authors thought about the end of the world.

Wells introduced the concept of a technologically superior, hostile alien race (Martians) pushing humanity to the brink of extinction. He intended it as a direct commentary on British colonialism, forcing Victorian readers to imagine how it felt to be on the receiving end of an overwhelming, technologically unstoppable invasion force. He further expressed his disdain for those in power by having the apocalypse averted by the smallest entities on Earth — bacteria. The Martians have no immunity to Earth's microbes & succumb to infection.
media-books-Forster:
[Back]
In this novel, humanity lives underground, entirely dependent on an all-powerful, automated global machine. When the machine inevitably breaks down, humanity collapses with it.

This is arguably the most prophetic sci-fi story ever written. Forster predicted the internet, instant messaging, video calls, & a society completely paralyzed by its over-reliance on technology.
media-books-London:
[Back]
In this novella, a sudden, uncontrollable pandemic called the 'Red Death' wipes out almost the entire global population in 2013. Some 60 years later, an old survivor is trying to explain the lost world of high technology, universities, & air travel to his savage, tribal grandsons who have no concept of civilization.
media-books-Harbou:
[Back]
Later made into the famous film Metropolis, this book depicts a dystopian apocalypse where the division between the wealthy elites & the subterranean working class threatens to violently tear society apart.
media-books-shape:
[Back]
This story is framed as the notes of a deceased diplomat, Dr Philip Raven, who experienced vivid, chronological dreams of a history textbook published in the 22nd century.
It predicts:

  • in 1940, a devastating, decades-long world war breaking out in Europe, leading to economic collapse & total social breakdown;
  • then a global plague called the 'wandering sickness' decimates half the human population;
  • by 1965, civilization is saved by a benevolent, elite group of pilots & mechanics called the 'Benevolent Bourgeoisie' or 'The Air Dictatorship' operating from bases in Iraq to control aircraft;
  • this dictatorship uses a sleep-inducing gas called 'Pacificin' to suppress local warlords, eliminate traditional nations & establish a single world government.
  • by 2106, a utopian, classless global state exists where humanity has conquered war, disease & poverty, shifting its focus toward scientific progress & space exploration.
media-books-Stewart:
[Back]
This was an influential novel about a scholar attempting to rebuild society after a disease wipes out most of humanity.
media-books-Wyndham:
[Back]
Wyndham's novel is a masterpiece of British science fiction. It is famous for creating the 'cosy catastrophe' subgenre, where society collapses but a small group of middle-class survivors attempts to rebuild.
media-books-Matheson:
[Back]
This atory was a massive influence on modern zombie apocalypse stories, depicting a lone survivor in a world of infected creatures.
media-books-Shute:
[Back]
On the Beach was a defining novel of the Cold War era that tracks the final months of the last humans (in Australia) waiting for deadly global nuclear radiation to reach them.
media-books-Miller:
[Back]
A Hugo Award-winning masterpiece tracking a Catholic monastery over thousands of years as humanity rebuilds from a nuclear holocaust, only to face the same cycle again.
media-books-King:
[Back]
A monumental epic about a weaponised strain of influenza that kills 99% of the population, followed by a biblical battle between good & evil.
media-books-Atwood:
[Back]
A dystopian & apocalyptic scenario where environmental collapse & infertility lead to a totalitarian regime.
media-books-James:
[Back]
A novel focusing on a world facing sudden mass infertility, exploring the psychological despair of a society with no future generations.
media-books-McCarthy:
[Back]
This Pulitzer Prize-winning novel that stripped the genre of sci-fi tropes. It follows a father & son through a burned, ash-covered, post-apocalyptic American landscape.
media-books-Brooks:
[Back]
This was an influential epistolary novel that treated a zombie apocalypse as a global geopolitical & bureaucratic crisis.
media-radio:
[Back]
Numerous famous apocalyptic radio broadcasts were adaptations of pre-existing novels, including:

  • The War of the Worlds (CBS, Mercury Theatre on the Air, 30 Oct 1938)
  • Earth Abides (CBS, Escape, 5 & 12 Nov 1950)
  • The Day of the Triffids (BBC, 1953, 1968 & 2001)
  • The Scarlet Plague (NBC, Escape, 8 Apr 1954)
  • A Canticle for Leibowitz (Wisconsin Public Radio / NPR, 1981)
  • On the Beach (BBC Radio, Nov 2008)

Other 'original' apocalyptic radio shows include:
  • The Fifth Horseman (NBC Radio, 1946)
  • The Peoria Plague (WUHN Radio, early 1970s)
  • The Last Broadcast (released online, 2020s)

Other than Orson Welles' War of the Worlds, most radio productions played to relatively small audiences (less than 1 million). However, their cultural footprint has been amplified over time by repeats, CD releases & streaming so their cumulative audiences & cultural impacts over decades are much larger than the original broadcast figures would indicate.
media-radio-Wells:
[Back]
Orson Welles narrated this production, an adaptation of Wells' novel, on Halloween in 1938. It was staged as breaking news about a Martian invasion. Heard by over 6 million people, itt became infamous for convincing some (reportedly about 1 million) the invasion was actually occurring & causing significant panic.
media-radio-London:
[Back]
Based on London's post-apocalyptic tale of a global plague, it was dramatised for radio as a chilling 'what comes after' story.
media-radio-Stewart:
[Back]
This was broadcast as a two-part dramatisation of Stewart's novel about a survivor after a global epidemic destroys civilization.
media-radio-Wyndham:
[Back]
The BBC produced 3 full cast dramatisations of Wyndham's post-war 'science fantasy' about a world blinded by a meteor shower then overrun by mobile, predatory plants. These included:

  • a BBC Light Programme production (adapted by Giles Cooper) in 1957 (6 30-minute episodes).
  • a BBC Radio 4 production in 1968 based on the same Giles Cooper adaptation (6 30-minute episodes). It was later eleased on CD as part of the 'Classic Radio Sci-Fi' series.
  • a BBC World Service production based on a new adaptation by Lance Dann (2 45-minute episodes).

In addition, the BBC periodically recorded & broadcast readings from this influential & popular book over more than 50 years, including:
  • 1953 - BBC Home Service broadcast 15 15-minute readings by Frank Duncan.
  • 1971 - BBC Radio 4 broadcast 10 15-minute readings by Gabriel Woolf.
  • 1973 - BBC Radio 4 (schools) broadcast a 20-minute extract adapted & produced by Peter Fozzard
  • 1980 - BBC Radio 4 (Woman's Hour) broadcast 14 15-minute readings by David Ashford.
  • 2004 on - BBC 7 produced a 17-part unabridged reading of the novel by Roger May; this was broadcast with many subsequent repeats on Radio 4 Extra.
media-radio-Miller:
[Back]
A dramatisation of Miller's novel about monks preserving knowledge through repeated cycles of post=apocalyptic collapse.
media-radio-Shute:
[Back]
The BBC produced & broadcast this dramatisation of Shute's novel in 2 episodes. It follows the novel's narrative about the aftermath of a nuclear war, focusing on characters awaiting inevitable fallout in Australia.
media-radio-horseman:
[Back]
This was a multi-part Cold War-era drama about nuclear crisis. It was created for radio in a post-war campaign to persuade the American public to support placing nuclear weapons under UN control.
media-radio-peoria:
[Back]
This was a local radio drama created by WUHN (now WSWT) in Peoria, Illinois in the early 1970s. It was done in 'War of the Worlds' style about a zombie-like outbreak, blending apocalyptic horror with faux-news bulletins.
media-radio-broadcast:
[Back]
This was a modern audio drama styled as a real-time global thermonuclear war broadcast, explicitly evoking Welles' technique & Cold War 'end of the world' anxiety.
media-tv:
[Back]
TV broadasting began in the mid-1930s, & early individual episodes in anthologies & serials were dedicated to exploring various apocalyptic & post-apocalyptic scenarios. For cultural, political & financial reasons, however, apocalyptic TV series only really began to appear from the 1950s, evolving over the subsequent decades alongside shifting geopolitical & cultural anxieties. Significant examples include:

  • Quatermass & the Pit (BBC, 1958–1959)
  • Out of the Unknown (BBC, 1965-1971)
  • Survivors (BBC, 1975-1977)
  • Battlestar Galactica (Various - 1978-2009)
  • The Stand (ABC, 1994)
  • Millennium (Fox, 1996-1999)
  • The Last Train (ITC, 1999)
  • Jericho (CBS, 2006-2008)
  • The Walking Dead (AMC, 2010-2022)
  • The Leftovers (HBO, 2014-2017)
  • Dark (Netflix, 2017-2020)
  • Station Eleven (Paramount, 2021)

While many of these series had a limited geographical reach through their initial regional, time-bound broadcasts, streaming platforms have transformed many of them into enduring global phenomena.
media-tv-anthologies:
[Back]
Significant examples include:

  • The Twilight Zone (1959-1964, 1985-1989, 2002-2003, 2019-2020) … all four incarnations of The Twilight Zone included episodes which portrayed apocalyptic threats, ranging from nuclear annihilation & impending environmental collapse to alien invasions & global psychological breakdown.
  • The Outer Limits (1963-1965, 1995-2002) … both the original & revival series of The Outer Limits frequently explored apocalyptic scenarios, driven heavily by hard sci-fi themes like runaway military technology, alien extermination campaigns, & nuclear doomsday devices.
media-tv-anthologies-twilight:
[Back]
Examples of apocalayptic episodes appear in each series, including:

  • Original Series (1959-1964)
  • First Revival (1985-1989)
  • Second Revival (2002-2003)
  • Third Revival (2019-2020)
media-tv-anthologies-twilight1:
[Back]
From the Original Series (1959-1964):

  • S1E8 - Time Enough at Last (1959): a bank teller survives a nuclear explosion inside a bank vault, only to face total human isolation.
  • S1E14 - Third from the Sun (1959): two families flee a planet on the brink of imminent nuclear destruction, only to escape to a new world called Earth.
  • S3E1 - Two (1961): two enemy soldiers navigate a destroyed city after an unnamed total war.
  • S3E3 - The Shelter (1961): suburban neighbours fight over a single fallout shelter amid rumours of a nuclear strike.
  • S3E8 - It's a Good Life (1961): a six-year-old boy with godlike reality-warping abilities who holds his isolated hometown of Peaksville, Ohio, hostage under the constant threat of being wished away to 'the cornfield.''.
  • S3E10 - The Midnight Sun (1961): Earth's orbit is disrupted, sending the planet hurtling toward the sun & causing civilization to collapse under catastrophic heating (until a twist reveals the opposite extreme).
  • S3E17 - One More Pallbearer (1961): a wealthy man creates a elaborate simulated nuclear apocalypse in a fallout shelter to force three people from his past to apologise.
  • S5E7 - The Old Man in the Cave (1963): a post-apocalyptic community relies on a mysterious computer to warn them of radiation-poisoned food.
  • S5E9 - Probe 7, Over & Out (1963): an astronaut stranded on a remote planet learns his home world has completely destroyed itself in a global war.
media-tv-anthologies-twilight2:
[Back]
From the First Revival Series (1985-1989):

  • S1E1a - A Little Peace & Quiet (1985): a harried housewife gains a pendant that stops time, ultimately using it at the exact instant a nuclear missile is about to detonate.
  • S1E18a - Gramma (1985): a young boy uncovers an ancient, eldritch threat capable of unleashing cosmic apocalypses, adapted from Stephen King's short story.
  • S2E7b - Shelter Skelter (1986): a survivalist builds a deep bomb shelter; after a nuclear blast occurs, he faces an existential predicament underground.
  • S3E16 - The Day Conversation Stopped (1961): global communication & human connection mysteriously break down, causing widespread societal collapses.
media-tv-anthologies-twilight3:
[Back]
From the Second Revival (2002-2003):

  • S1E14 - Harsh Mistress (2002): a musician buys an acoustic guitar that grants fame but drives its listeners to catastrophic madness & destruction.
  • S1E31 - It's Still a Good Life (2003): a direct sequel to the 1961 classic, where Anthony's godlike powers continue to keep the surviving remnant of Peaksville isolated from a ruined world..
media-tv-anthologies-twilight4:
[Back]
From the Third Revival (2019-2020):

  • S1E4 - A Traveler (2019): a mysterious stranger appears at an Alaskan police station during Christmas, manipulating paranoia to facilitate an extraterrestrial invasion.
  • S2E10 - You Might Also Like (2020): Society becomes obsessed with a mysterious device called the 'Egg' which turns out to be a sinister alien tool designed to pacify & reshape Earth.
media-tv-anthologies-limits:
[Back]
Examples of apocalyptic episodes in The Outer Limits appear in both series

  • Original Series (1963-1965)
  • Revival Series (1995-2002)
media-tv-anthologies-limits1:
[Back]
From the Original Series (1963-1965,):

  • S1E3 - The Architects of Fear (1963): facing global nuclear annihilation, scientists surgically transform one of their own into a terrifying alien threat to forcibly unite humanity against a common, fabricated enemy.
  • S1E14 - The Mice (1963): a teleporter exchange program with an alien species backfires when the aliens turn out to be an invasive vanguard sent to harvest humanity.
  • S2E1 - Soldier (1964): two soldiers from 1,800 years in the future—born into a world entirely consumed & ruined by apocalyptic warfare—are accidentally hurled back in time to modern Earth.
  • S2E5 - Demon with a Glass Hand (1964): a solitary man wanders a deserted Earth, only to discover humanity has been wiped out/archived to escape an invading alien force known as the Kyben.
media-tv-anthologies-limits2:
[Back]
From the Revival Series (1995-2002):

  • S1E14 - The Quality of Mercy (1995) + S2E18 - The Light Brigade (1996): key chapters in an overarching story arc depicting a desperate intergalactic war where Earth faces imminent extinction from an aggressive alien species (the Kyben).
  • S2E1 - A Stitch in Time (1996): a scientist uses a time machine to assassinate historical serial killers before their rampages, inadvertently altering timelines & triggering a nuclear apocalyptic future.
  • S2E12 - Inconstant Moon (1996): people on Earth realize that the moon glowing with unprecedented brightness means the sun has gone nova, signaling the immediate end of all life on the daylight side of Earth.
  • S3E13 - Dead Man's Switch (1997): operators in underground bunkers across the globe are tasked with holding down dead-man switches to prevent the automated launch of doomsday weapons aimed at an invading alien force.
  • S5E13 - The Apocalypse (1999): a group of scientists investigates a mysterious message that triggers global apocalyptic phenomena, bringing humanity to the edge of total collapse.
  • S7E20 - Human Trials (2001): soldiers undergo brutal psychological & physical evaluations to earn a spot on a mission designed to preserve human life after Earth is rendered uninhabitable.
media-tv-serials:
[Back]
The most enduring example is Dr Who (1963-present). The early series regularly featured devastated, post-apocalyptic worlds, including:

  • The Daleks (1963) introduced Skaro as a nuclear wasteland ruined by a planetary war between the Thals & Daleks … this was a direct allegory for Cold War MAD (Mutually Assured Destruction) policy
  • The Dalek Invasion of Earth (1964) … in AD 2164, meteor strikes unleash a plague that wipes out millions, allowing Daleks to invade Eath, enslave the remaining human population & strip-mine Earth's core. Among the most famous early episodes, it features eerie shots of a ruined, desolate London.
  • The Ark (1966) … the Sun expands & humanity survives on a massive generation ship (The Ark) carrying frozen embryos & the last remnants of terrestrial life.
  • Inferno (1970) … a drilling project pierces Earth's crust, unleashing toxic gas & molten core, while in a parallel dimension, the Doctor sees the drill succeed & cause a volcanic apocalypse that completely destroys that version of Earth.
media-tv-Quatermass:
[Back]
Quatermass & the Pit (BBC, 1958-1959): Workers unearth a mysterious, ancient metallic object during a London excavation. Professor Bernard Quatermass investigates & uncovers a terrifying truth: the artifact is an ancient Martian spacecraft, revealing that humanity's evolutionary history & latent psychic abilities stem from pre-historic alien genetic engineering.
media-tv-unknown:
[Back]
A flagship British science-fiction anthology series that adapted high-concept short stories by legendary authors like Isaac Asimov, Ray Bradbury, & J.G. Ballard. The show tackled speculative technology, dystopian societies, artificial intelligence, & psychological existential dread.
media-tv-Survivors:
[Back]
Survivors (BBC, 1975–1977): Created by Terry Nation, this gritty drama follows a handful of survivors in the aftermath of 'The Death', a fast-spreading, accidental plague that wipes out 99% of the world's population. The series focuses on the practical, psychological, & moral struggles of rebuilding a agrarian society from scratch.
media-tv-galactica:
[Back]
Battlestar Galactica (Numerous series - ABC, 1978-1979; ABC, 1980 (as Galactica); Sci Fi Channel, 2003; Universal, 2004-2009): Following the total annihilation of humanity's Twelve Colonies by the cybernetic Cylons, the military aircraft carrier Galactica leads a makeshift fleet of civilian survivors across deep space in a desperate search for a legendary thirteenth colony: Earth.
media-tv-stand:
[Back]
The Stand (ABC, 1994): Based on Stephen King's epic novel, a weaponized strain of influenza dubbed 'Captain Trips' accidentally escapes a lab & kills almost the entire global population. The remaining immune survivors are drawn into a supernatural confrontation between the benevolent Mother Abagail & the demonic Randall Flagg.
media-tv-millenium:
[Back]
Millennium (Fox, 1996–1999): Created by Chris Carter, this dark procedural centers on Frank Black, a former FBI profiler with the uncanny ability to see into the minds of killers. Working for the mysterious Millennium Group, he investigates horrific crimes as apocalyptic omens as the turn of the 21st century approaches.
media-tv-train:
[Back]
The Last Train (ITV/ITC, 1999): A group of commuters on a train heading to Sheffield are accidentally frozen in cryogenic gas during a runaway collision. They awaken decades later to discover a post-apocalyptic, overgrown Britain devastated by a disastrous asteroid strike.
media-tv-jericho:
[Back]
Jericho (CBS, 2006–2008): The residents of a small, isolated Kansas town are thrown into chaos after seeing mushroom clouds on the horizon, cutting them off from the rest of the world. The town must band together to manage limited resources, social collapse, & political fallout following coordinated nuclear strikes across major U.S. cities.
media-tv-walking:
[Back]
Based on the comic series, deputy sherriff Rick Grimes wakes from a coma into a world overrun by flesh-eating zombies ('walkers'). He leads a fluctuating group of survivors who face constant death, shifting social orders, & the realization that surviving humans are often far more dangerous than the undead.
media-tv-leftovers:
[Back]
The Leftovers (HBO, 2014-2017): Three years after the inexplicable 'Sudden Departure' — in which 2% of the world's population vanishes simultaneously — the remaining population struggles to cope with the overwhelming grief, religious extremism, existential angst, & complete breakdown of traditional societal norms.
media-tv-dark:
[Back]
Dark (Netflix, 2017-2020): The disappearance of a child in a small German town uncovers a sprawling, multigenerational time-travel conspiracy centered around a local nuclear power plant, intertwining four families across decades as they try to prevent an impending, world-ending apocalypse bound in a temporal loop.
media-tv-station:
[Back]
Station Eleven (HBO Max/Paramount, 2021): Spanning multiple timelines before, during, & 20 years after a devastating flu pandemic wipes out civilization, the story follows the 'Traveling Symphony' — a troupe of actors & musicians keeping art & culture alive — as they cross paths with a mysterious cult.
media-movies:
[Back]
Apocalyptic films made for cinema & TV have repeatedly reflected cultural fears of their period. Early films imagined comets, plagues, floods & cosmic collisions; the Cold War brought nuclear annihilation to the centre of the genre; later films explored ecological collapse, pandemics, AI, terrorism, zombies & social breakdown.

Significant examples appear in almost every decade since 1920:

  • the 1910s
  • the 1920s
  • the 1930s
  • the 1940s
  • the 1950s
  • the 1960s
  • the 1970s
  • the 1980s
  • the 1990s
  • the 2000s
  • the 2010s
  • the 2020s
media-movies-1910s:
[Back]
The most significant example was:
The End of the World (1916, cinema).
Also known as The Flaming Sword, this Danish film depicts a worldwide catastrophe when a comet passes by Earth, causing natural disasters & social unrest. It attracted a huge audience due to fears around the passing of Halley's Comet in 1910 & the ongoing unrest of WW1.
media-movies-1920s:
[Back]
Significant examples include:

  • The Last Man on Earth< (1924, cinema).
  • Metropolis< (1927, cinema).
media-movies-lastman1924:
[Back]
A virus kills almost every man over the age of fourteen, leaving one apparent male survivor. The film reflects early twentieth-century fears of epidemic disease, demographic collapse & the disappearance of social order.
media-movies-metropolis1927:
[Back]
Fritz Lang's expressionist film was based on the 1925 novel Metropolis by Thea von Harbou. It presents a technologically advanced city divided between wealthy rulers above ground & exploited workers below it. Its apocalyptic imagery centres on industrial dehumanisation, social revolution & the destruction threatened by uncontrolled technology.
media-movies-1930s:
[Back]
Significant examples include:

  • La Fin du Monde (The End of the World) (1931, cinema)
  • Deluge (1933, cinema)
  • Things to Come (1936, cinema)
  • The War of the Worlds (1938, TV)
media-movies-end1931:
[Back]
Abel Gance's French film was based on the 1894 novel La Fin du Monde by Camille Flammarion. It follows the discovery of a comet on a collision course with Earth. It combines cosmic catastrophe with political conflict & public disbelief, continuing the early cinema tradition of imagining nature as the agent of civilisation's destruction.
media-movies-deluge1933:
[Back]
Based on the 1928 novel Deluge by S. Fowler Wright, this movie shows a series of earthquakes & a gigantic flood that devastate the United States. The surviving characters face displacement, violence & the struggle to establish a new community, making this an important early example of the disaster & post-apocalyptic film.
media-movies-things1936:
[Back]
Adapted from H.G. Wells's The Shape of Things to Come, this film imagines a future world destroyed by war, plague & social collapse before being rebuilt under a technocratic world government. It contrasts destructive nationalism with the promise & danger of scientific progress.
media-movies-war1938:
[Back]
This early television adaptation of H.G. Wells's 1898 alien-invasion story helped establish the possibility of presenting an apocalyptic drama through the new broadcast medium. It belongs to the same cultural tradition as the much more famous 1938 radio production.
media-movies-1950s:
[Back]
Significant examples include:

  • Five (1951, cinema)
  • When Worlds Collide (1951, cinema)
  • The War of the Worlds (1953, cinema)
  • Day the World Ended (1955, cinema)
  • Invasion of the Body Snatchers (1956, cinema)
  • The World, the Flesh and the Devil (1959, cinema)
  • On the Beach (1959, cinema)
media-movies-five1951:
[Back]
After a nuclear war, five people appear to be the only survivors in the United States. The film is unusually intimate for its period, concentrating on suspicion, racism, sexual threat & the ethical choices involved in rebuilding human society.
media-movies-worlds1951:
[Back]
Based on the 1933 science fiction novel When Worlds Collide by Edwin Balmer & Philip Wylie, the movie shows scientists discovering that another planet is on a collision course with Earth. A selected group constructs a spacecraft to escape, while the rest of humanity faces extinction. The film combines scientific speculation with the moral question of who should be saved.
media-movies-war1953:
[Back]
This influential adaptation transforms Wells's Victorian Martians from his 1898 novel into technologically overwhelming invaders attacking Cold War America. Humanity's survival ultimately depends not on superior weapons but on the biological vulnerability of the invaders.
media-movies-day1955:
[Back]
A nuclear war leaves a small group of survivors in an isolated region. Mutated creatures & the collapse of civilisation turn the film into a bleak combination of atomic-horror & post-apocalyptic survival story.
media-movies-body1956:
[Back]
Based on the 1954 novel by Jack Finney, this film shows alien spores replacing sleeping humans with emotionless duplicates. Although the film does not show a conventional destroyed world, its apocalypse is the gradual loss of human identity, individuality & resistance to total social conformity.
media-movies-world1959:
[Back]
Loosely based on the 1901 novel The Purple Cloud by M.P. Shiel, this movie shows a miner emerging from an underground collapse & discovers that almost everyone has died after a nuclear holocaust. The film explores loneliness, interracial cooperation & the possibility of rebuilding society without the institutions that previously divided humanity.
media-movies-beach1959:
[Back]
Stanley Kramer's adaptation of Nevil Shute's 1957 novel follows Australians & visiting Americans during the final months after nuclear war has spread lethal radiation across the world. Its quiet, deterministic treatment of extinction made it one of the defining anti-nuclear films of the Cold War.
media-movies-1960s:
[Back]
Significant examples include:

  • The Day the Earth Caught Fire (1961, cinema)
  • Panic in Year Zero! (1962, cinema)
  • Dr. Strangelove (1964, cinema)
  • Fail Safe (1964, cinema)
  • The War Game (1965, TV)
  • The Bed Sitting Room (1969, cinema)
media-movies-earth1961:
[Back]
Nuclear tests alter the Earth's rotation & drive the planet toward catastrophic climate change. The film links military technology with planetary instability & uses its newsroom setting to examine denial, scientific uncertainty & public panic.
media-movies-war1962:
[Back]
This television drama depicts ordinary Americans reacting to reports of an approaching nuclear attack. Its emphasis is not on military strategy but on confusion, fear & the rapid breakdown of everyday assumptions.
media-movies-strangelove1964:
[Back]
Stanley Kubrick's dark satire follows an absurd chain of military decisions that threatens global nuclear annihilation. Its comedy exposes the irrationality of deterrence systems controlled by institutions, technology & personalities.
media-movies-failsafe1964:
[Back]
A technical error sends American bombers toward Moscow, while political & military leaders struggle to prevent an accidental nuclear war. Unlike the comic treatment in Dr Strangelove, this film presents the same basic danger as a tense tragedy.
media-movies-war1965:
[Back]
Produced by the BBC as a fictional documentary, this film depicts the consequences of a nuclear attack on Britain. It presents the collapse of public services, health care, food distribution & civil authority in an intentionally unsensational style.
media-movies-bed1969:
[Back]
In this adaptation of the 1963 play The Bed-Sitting Room by Spike Milligan & John Antrobus, survivors in Britain after a nuclear war live among ruins & radioactive contamination. The film uses absurdist comedy to expose the inadequacy of official optimism & the persistence of class, bureaucracy & human folly after catastrophe.
media-movies-1970s:
[Back]
Significant examples include:

  • Zardoz (1974, cinema)
  • A Boy and His Dog (1975, cinema)
  • Logan's Run (1976, cinema)
  • Mad Max (1979, cinema)
media-movies-zardoz1974:
[Back]
In a distant post-apocalyptic future, humanity is divided between immortal elites & impoverished outsiders. The film treats social inequality, technological immortality & the loss of purpose as consequences of a civilisation that has survived physically but failed spiritually.
media-movies-boy1975:
[Back]
After nuclear war, a young man & his intelligent dog travel through a violent & sexually oppressive wasteland. Based on the 1969 novella A Boy & His Dog by Harlan Ellison, the film is a dark satire of militarism, slavery, survival ethics & the possibility that civilisation may not deserve to be restored.
media-movies-logans1976:
[Back]
Survivors of an earlier catastrophe live in a sealed, technologically managed city where people are required to die at thirty. Based on the 1967 novel by William F. Nolan & George Clayton Johnson, the film presents a population protected from external dangers at the cost of freedom, historical memory & responsibility.
media-movies-mad1979:
[Back]
Set during the early stages of social collapse, Mad Max depicts a near-future Australia where violence, fuel scarcity & failing institutions threaten ordinary life. It helped establish the visual language of the modern post-apocalyptic road film.
media-movies-1980s:
[Back]
Significant examples include:

  • Mad Max 2: The Road Warrior (1981, cinema)
  • The Day After (1983, TV)
  • Threads (1984, TV)
  • The Terminator (1984, cinema)
  • Mad Max Beyond Thunderdome (1985, cinema)
  • When the Wind Blows (1986, cinema)
media-movies-mad2:
[Back]
In a desert wasteland after civilisation's collapse, a community protects its remaining fuel from marauding gangs. The film's emphasis on water, mobility, barter, violence & fragile cooperation became highly influential throughout post-apocalyptic cinema.
media-movies-after1983:
[Back]
This American television film portrays the effects of a large-scale nuclear exchange on residents of a Midwestern community. It brought the consequences of nuclear war into millions of homes & became a major public discussion point during the final decade of the Cold War.
media-movies-threads1984:
[Back]
This BBC television film follows two Sheffield families before, during & after a nuclear exchange. Its documentary-like treatment of radiation sickness, famine, social disintegration & generational decline is among the most uncompromising depictions of nuclear apocalypse.
media-movies-terminator1984:
[Back]
An artificial intelligence called Skynet initiates a nuclear war & then attempts to exterminate the human survivors. The film combines time travel & action cinema with an enduring warning about autonomous military technology.
media-movies-mad3:
[Back]
Max encounters a settlement attempting to preserve electricity, trade & social organisation in the ruins of Australia. The film is less bleak than its predecessors & focuses more explicitly on the possibility of rebuilding a functioning community.
media-movies-prince1986:
[Back]
Based on Raymond Briggs's graphic novel, this animated film follows an elderly British couple who trust official assurances that they can survive a nuclear war. Its restrained domestic perspective makes the destruction especially disturbing.
media-movies-1990s:
[Back]
Significant examples include:

  • The Last Man on Earth (1990, TV)
  • 12 Monkeys (1995, cinema)
  • Independence Day (1996, cinema)
  • Armageddon (1998, cinema)
  • Deep Impact (1998, cinema)
  • The Matrix (1999, cinema)
media-movies-lastman1990:
[Back]
This television adaptation of Richard Matheson's I Am Legend (1954) presents a lone survivor in a world devastated by plague. The story helped connect pandemic apocalypse with the modern vampire & zombie traditions.
media-movies-twelve1995:
[Back]
A deadly virus has nearly destroyed humanity, & a prisoner is sent back through time to investigate its origin. Inspired by Chris Marker's 1962 featurette La Jetée, the film combines pandemic catastrophe, unreliable memory, time loops & the question of whether history can be changed.
media-movies-day1996:
[Back]
An alien invasion attacks major cities around the world. Although presented as spectacular entertainment, the film revived the classic invasion-apocalypse scenario & places global cooperation at the centre of humanity's survival.
media-movies-armageddon1998:
[Back]
A team of oil-drillers is sent into space to destroy an asteroid heading toward Earth. The film turns planetary defence into a heroic disaster adventure focused on sacrifice, teamwork & the survival of the human species.
media-movies-deep1998:
[Back]
Scientists & astronauts attempt to prevent an asteroid impact by drilling into it & detonating a nuclear device. Compared with Armageddon, the film gives greater attention to government planning, public communication & the emotional consequences of choosing who may survive.
media-movies-matrix1999:
[Back]
Humanity has been defeated by intelligent machines & is kept in a simulated reality while its bodies are used as an energy source. The apocalypse is therefore both physical & epistemological: people must discover that the world they experience is constructed & controlled.
media-movies-2000s:
[Back]
Significant examples include:

  • 28 Days Later (2002, cinema)
  • Signs (2002, cinema)
  • Dawn of the Dead (2004, cinema)
  • The Day After Tomorrow (2004, cinema)
  • War of the Worlds (2005, cinema)
  • Children of Men (2006, cinema)
  • The Road (2009, cinema)
  • Knowing (2009, cinema)
media-movies-days2002:
[Back]
A rage virus causes the collapse of British society within days. The film helped revive modern zombie cinema while presenting infection, quarantine, loneliness & human brutality as equally significant threats.
media-movies-signs2002:
[Back]
An alien invasion is experienced largely through the restricted viewpoint of a rural family. The film uses the threatened apocalypse to explore grief, providence, family reconciliation & the search for meaning after personal catastrophe.
media-movies-dawn2004:
[Back]
A zombie outbreak drives survivors into a shopping mall. The remake combines action horror with a critique of consumer culture, while showing how temporary safety can become another form of imprisonment.
media-movies-day2004:
[Back]
Human-induced climate change triggers abrupt global cooling & a new ice age. The film converts environmental anxiety into a large-scale disaster spectacle, with political decisions & family loyalty driving the survival narrative.
media-movies-war2005:
[Back]
Steven Spielberg's adaptation of Wells 1989 novel presents an alien invasion through the experience of an ordinary father trying to protect his children. Its images of evacuation, social panic & unexplained mass displacement also echo modern fears of terrorism & global insecurity.
media-movies-children2006:
[Back]
Based on the 1992 novel The Children of Men by P.D. James, the movie show humanity having become infertile & the youngest generation has died out. Set amid authoritarian government, refugee persecution & political violence, the film presents demographic extinction as a slow apocalypse that destroys hope before it destroys the population.
media-movies-road2009:
[Back]
A father & son travel through a burned & ash-covered landscape after an unnamed catastrophe. Adapted from Cormac McCarthy’s 2006 novel, the film strips away most scientific explanation & concentrates on moral endurance, compassion & the struggle to carry goodness through a ruined world.
media-movies-knowing2009:
[Back]
A sequence of numbers appears to predict major disasters & the deaths of millions. The story combines scientific investigation, solar catastrophe, determinism & a religiously suggestive account of preservation beyond the destruction of Earth.
media-movies-2010s:
[Back]
Significant examples include:

  • The Book of Eli (2010, cinema)
  • Contagion (2011, cinema)
  • Melancholia (2011, cinema)
  • World War Z (2013, cinema)
  • Snowpiercer (2013, cinema)
  • Interstellar (2014, cinema)
  • Mad Max: Fury Road (2015, cinema)
  • Arrival (2016, cinema)
  • Train to Busan (2016, cinema)
media-movies-book2010:
[Back]
After a war has devastated the United States, a solitary traveller protects a precious book while crossing a violent wasteland. The film uses biblical imagery to connect literacy, faith, moral responsibility & the preservation of civilisation.
media-movies-contagion2011:
[Back]
A novel virus spreads rapidly through international travel & overwhelms health systems. Its emphasis on epidemiology, public communication, misinformation & social cooperation makes it one of the most realistic modern pandemic films.
media-movies-melancholia2011:
[Back]
A rogue planet approaches Earth on a collision course. The film treats planetary extinction through the psychological experiences of several characters, contrasting social ceremony & personal anxiety with the indifference of cosmic destruction.
media-movies-world2013:
[Back]
A rapidly spreading infection turns people into violent attackers & brings governments close to collapse. Loosely based on the 2006 novel by Max Brooks, the film presents the crisis as a global logistical & military emergency rather than focusing only on individual survival.
media-movies-snowpiercer2013:
[Back]
This film is based on the French graphic novel Le Transperceneige by Jacques Lob, Benjamin Legrand & Jean-Marc Rochette. An attempt to reverse global warming freezes the planet has left the last survivors aboard a continuously moving train. The train's rigid class structure becomes a miniature image of civilisation, linking environmental catastrophe with inequality & revolution.
media-movies-interstellar2014:
[Back]
Environmental collapse makes Earth increasingly unable to support human life. Astronauts search for a habitable world while the film explores time, sacrifice, family love, scientific courage & humanity's responsibility to future generations.
media-movies-mad2015:
[Back]
In a water-starved desert society ruled by a violent dictator, survivors attempt to escape toward a more hopeful community. Its apocalyptic world combines resource scarcity, patriarchal power, ecological ruin & the possibility of collective liberation.
media-movies-arrival2016:
[Back]
Alien vessels appear around Earth & international governments risk interpreting contact as an act of war. Based on Ted Chiang’s 1998 novella Story of Your Life, the film treats apocalypse as a failure of communication & suggests that linguistic understanding & cooperation may prevent global destruction.
media-movies-train2016:
[Back]
A zombie outbreak begins during a train journey across South Korea. Confined spaces, social class, parental love & self-sacrifice shape the passengers' attempt to survive while the wider country collapses.
media-movies-2020s:
[Back]
Significant examples include:

  • Don't Look Up (2021, cinema)
  • Leave the World Behind (2023, cinema)
media-movies-dont2021:
[Back]
Two astronomers discover a comet that will destroy Earth, but political leaders, news media & the public treat the warning as entertainment or partisan controversy. The film satirises denial, distraction, commercialisation & the inability to respond collectively to an obvious catastrophe.
media-movies-leave2023:
[Back]
Based on the 2020 novel Leave the World Behind by Rumaan Alam, the film portrays a family holiday being disrupted by a nationwide communications & infrastructure failure. The film leaves the exact cause uncertain while exploring technological dependence, social mistrust, misinformation & the fragility of supposedly secure modern life.
